संदेश
मुझेसेवारत,सेवानिवृत्तकार्मिकोंतथाहमारेमृतकएवंवीरबलिदानियोंके
निकटतमपरिजनोंकेलिए“कल्यााणकारीयोजनाओंकीपुस्ति
का”केइससंशोधित
संकलनकोप्रस्तुतकरतेहुएबहुतप्रसन्नताहोरहीहै।यहप्रकाशनबलकेकार्मिकों
एवं उनके परिवारों के कल्यााण के प्रति हमारी अटूट प्रतिबद्धता को दर्शाता है।
सीआरपीएफकेकर्तव्योंोंकीचुनौतीपूर्णप्रकृतिकोध्यानमेंरखतेहुए,यह
पुस्ति
का सभी रैंकों केलिएवित्तीय एवंकल्यााणकारीयोजनाओसेसंबंधितअद्यतन
एवं आवश्यक जानकारी को संक्षिप्त रूप में उपलब्ध कराएगी। किसी भी
कल्यााणकारीयोजनाकीवास्तविकसफलताउसकेसमयवप्रभावीक्रि
यान्वयनपर
निर्भर करती है। मैंसभीकार्यालयप्रमुखोंसेयहआग्रहकरताहूँँकिइनमहत्वपूर्ण
जानकारियों का प्रसार सैनिक सम्मेेलनों एवं परिवार कल्यााण केंद्रों के माध्यम से
सुनिश्चित किया जाए, ताकि इसकी जानकारी देश से सबसेअग्रिमवदूरस्थतैनाती
वाले परिचालनिक बेसोंमें तैनातजवानोतकनिर्बाधरूपसेपहुँचसके।हमेंअपने
मृतक, वीर बलिदानियों के परिवारों एवं सेवानिवृत्त कार्मिकों को मार्गदर्शन प्रदान

[केरिपुबल कल्याण पुस्तिका | Chapter 00 | Page 2]
रिचालनिक बेसोंमें तैनातजवानोतकनिर्बाधरूपसेपहुँचसके।हमेंअपने
मृतक, वीर बलिदानियों के परिवारों एवं सेवानिवृत्त कार्मिकों को मार्गदर्शन प्रदान
करने मे प्राथमिकता देनी चाहिए, ताकि वेअपनीआवश्यकताओंकोसहजता एवं
गरिमा के साथ पूर्ण कर सकें।
मैं श्रीी पॉली पी.पी., उपमहानिरीक्षक (कल्यााण), सभी अधिकारियों एवं
कार्मिको को इस महत्वपूर्ण दस्तावेज़ को अद्यतन करने हेतु उनके प्रयासों की
सराहनाकरताहूँँ।निरंतरसहायताकीसंस्कृृतिकोबढ़ाावादेतेहुए,हमसीआरपीएफ
के आदर्श वाक्य - “सेवाएवंनिष्ठाा”केप्रतिअपनीप्रतिबद्धताकोपुनःदोहरातेहैं।
मुझेविश्वाासहैकियहपुस्ति
काएकत्वरितमार्गदर्शिकाकेरूपमेंकार्यकरेगीतथा
राष्ट्रकीसेवामेंसमर्पितजवानोकेभविष्यकोसशक्तएवंसुरक्षितबनानेमेंसहायक
सिद्ध होगी। जय हिन्द ।
(जी.पी. सिंंह)
महानिदेशक

About Ayushman CAPF 
1. What is Ayushman CAPF? 
Ayushman CAPF is a cashless health insurance scheme for serving CAPF personnel and their 
dependents. It’s a joint initiative of the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) and the National Health 
Authority (NHA). This scheme is being implemented on National Health Authority’s IT platform. 
Under the scheme cashless healthcare benefits can be availed across all HCOs empanelled with NHA. 
2. When was the Ayushman CAPF launched? 
Ayushman CAPF was launched by Hon’ble Home Minister on 23rd January 2021 in Assam. 
Coverage 
3. Who can get benefits of this scheme? 
All the serving personnel and their dependents from seven forces, viz. Assam Rifles, Border Security 
Force (BSF), Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB), Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), Central Industrial 
Security Force (CISF), National Security Guard (NSG), and Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) are

[Ayushman CAPF Official FAQ | Page 4]

Security Force (CISF), National Security Guard (NSG), and Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) are 
entitled to avail cashless healthcare services in CGHS empanelled HCOs and private HCOs empanelled 
under PM-JAY. 

4. What is the geographical coverage currently? 
The scheme has been rolled out across the country in CGHS empanelled private hospitals which have 
signed MoU with NHA, and all private hospitals empanelled under AB PM-JAY scheme. 

5. What services are covered under Ayushman CAPF scheme? 
The following service are covered under Ayushman CAPF scheme as per the HCO type.

6. Where can a beneficiary get the Ayushman CAPF card from?

This is one time activity. 

7. Is there any other way for a beneficiary to get the Ayushman CAPF card? 
Alternatively, print out of Ayushman CAPF card can be obtained at empanelled private HCO. Serving 
CAPF personnel or their dependent would be required to submit the copy of the Force ID along with 
any Government approved Photo ID/Aadhaar card for issuance of Ayushman CAPF card printout at 
the HCO. 

8. How can a beneficiary get the Ayushman CAPF card activated? 
The Ayushman CAPF physical cards would need to be activated at empanelled private HCO. For this, 
PMAM of the HCO would do e-KYC authentication of the beneficiary in the Beneficiary Identification 
System (BIS) of NHA. For this, beneficiary needs to provide a copy of Force ID and Aadhaar or 
Government approved photo ID.

[Ayushman CAPF Official FAQ | Page 5]
ficiary Identification 
System (BIS) of NHA. For this, beneficiary needs to provide a copy of Force ID and Aadhaar or 
Government approved photo ID. 

9. What should the beneficiary do if the details on the Ayushman CAPF card / E-Card, such as name, 
date of birth, are wrong? 
Beneficiary needs to contact designated officials of their respective force to get such details 
corrected. The NHA IT platforms do not allow any change in beneficiary data. 

10. What should the beneficiary do if they lose the Ayushman CAPF Card? 
Print out of Ayushman CAPF card can be obtained from PMAM of any empanelled private HCOs. List 
of CGHS HCOs may be obtained at: 

https://cghs.gov.in/index1.php?page=1&ipp=All&lang=1&level=1&sublinkid=6760&lid=3704

11. Does the beneficiary need a new Ayushman CAPF card if my force or state is changed? 
Ayushman CAPF card will remain same even if personnel get transferred to other state. In case 
personnel goes on deputation to other force and force ID is changed then new Ayushman CAPF card 
will be issued. Previous Ayushman CAPF card will get disabled. 

12. What is the process for adding a new-born baby or a newly wedded spouse in the beneficiary 
database? 
Seven forces are the custodian of their beneficiary database. No change in the data is made at NHA 
level. Family members will be added/updated in the beneficiary database by the respective forces. 
Therefore, serving personnel needs to contact designated officials of their respective force.

13. Where can Ayushman CAPF beneficiaries complete their verification process? 
Pradhan Mantri Arogya Mitra (PMAM) in empanelled HCOs will do the beneficiary verification. 
Serving CAPF personnel or their dependent would be required to submit the copy of the 
Force/Dependent ID along with any Government approved Photo ID/Aadhaar card for one-time e-
KYC or beneficiary identification process. Upon verification of e-KYC, the CAPF beneficiaries can avail 
cashless health benefits at any of the empanelled CGHS HCO’s.

So, serving personnel and their dependents can also do the beneficiary verification at unit level. The

The Pradhan Mantri Arogya Mitra (PMAM) will be operating the BIS portal using the registered

16. What is required to avail cashless healthcare services in empanelled HCOs? 
Beneficiary need referral from any CAPF Hospital / Government Hospital and active Ayushman CAPF card 
to avail cashless healthcare services in empanelled HCOs. In case of emergency, Silver Card holders1 can 
also avail the services.

17. How can a beneficiary get help in an HCO for Ayushman CAPF scheme? 
Beneficiary needs to meet the Pradhan Mantri Arogya Mitra (PMAM) at the empaneled private HCO. 
PMAM will help beneficiary with all the queries like beneficiary verification, registration, hospitalization 
etc. The key responsibilities of the PMAM are as follows: 

1 Beneficiary who has Ayushman card but not undergone e-KYC authentication. Each card after e-KYC 
authentication is identified as Gold card by the IT system.

[Ayushman CAPF Official FAQ | Page 7]

a) Operating the Beneficiary Identification System (BIS) to identify and verify the beneficiaries entitled 
under Ayushman CAPF 
b) Guiding the beneficiary about the overall benefits under Ayushman CAPF and providing information 
about receiving prompt treatment at HCO 

18. Who is MEDCO? What is the role of MEDCO? 
MEDCO is the medical coordinator at the HCO, designated to look after clinical activities related to 
CAPF beneficiary. Her/his role is mainly to facilitate in ascertaining Diagnosis and blocking right 
package, raising intimation, Discharge & Claim Initiation etc. All these activities are done by MEDCO 
in coordination with treating doctor and Pradhan Mantri Arogya Mitra (PMAM)/HCO receptionist. 
19. Will all the beneficiaries need pre-authorization of a doctor for availing cashless healthcare services 
in HCO onboarded on NHA platform? 
MEDCO after registering the patient in TMS, raises the intimation to Pre-auth Panel Doctor (PPD) for

[Ayushman CAPF Official FAQ | Page 7]

in HCO onboarded on NHA platform? 
MEDCO after registering the patient in TMS, raises the intimation to Pre-auth Panel Doctor (PPD) for 
seeking approval on starting the treatment. OPD, emergency and patients aged more than 75 years, 
gets auto-approval to avoid any delay in the treatment. For all IPD patients, Pre-auth Panel Doctor 
(PPD) will process each case of intimation. 
20. How can beneficiary avail the medical treatment under Ayushman CAPF? 
a) For the self-paid services at CAPF or the government owned facilities (diagnostics, implants, 
medicines etc.), the CAPF serving personnel may submit a reimbursement request using CAPF 
Reimbursement Module. CAPF serving personnel can raise reimbursement claim of the expenses 
incurred for availing healthcare services for self and dependents. Please note that the 
reimbursement, when approved, will be as per CGHS rates. 
b) CAPF or the government owned facilities may refer the beneficiary to the CGHS and /or PM-JAY

[Ayushman CAPF Official FAQ | Page 7]
ursement, when approved, will be as per CGHS rates. 
b) CAPF or the government owned facilities may refer the beneficiary to the CGHS and /or PM-JAY 
empaneled private HCO. In this case, the beneficiary may avail cashless medical treatment by 
registering at the HCO using the activated Ayushman CAPF card. 
c) In case of emergency or in areas without empanelled hospital, the beneficiary may avail self-paid 
services at non-empaneled HCO and submit a reimbursement request using CAPF Reimbursement 
Module. Reimbursement, when approved, will be as per CGHS rates and guidelines.

## 1. Scope & Purpose
Payment of ex-gratia lump sum compensation to the families of Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) personnel who die in the performance of their bona fide official duties under various operational circumstances.

## 2. Compensation Slabs & Categories
1. **Death in Performance of Duties (Accidents / Natural Calamities):**
 - **Amount:** ₹25 Lakh.
 - Applies to deaths occurring during election deployment, natural disaster rescue operations, official travel accidents, or high-altitude terrain hazards not involving enemy action.
2. **Death in Border Clashes, Enemy Action, or Counter-Insurgency:**
 - **Amount:** ₹35 Lakh.

 - **Amount:** ₹45 Lakh.

- Paid 100% directly to the legally nominated Next of Kin (NoK) as recorded in the service book.

**Last Verified:** 2026-09-25

---

## 1. Objective & Mandate
Bharat Ke Veer is a trust established under the Ministry of Home Affairs to facilitate public and corporate financial contributions directly to the Next of Kin (NoK) of Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) personnel who have laid down their lives in the line of duty fighting terrorists, insurgents, or guarding international borders.

[Bharat Ke Veer Corpus Fund]
who have laid down their lives in the line of duty fighting terrorists, insurgents, or guarding international borders.

## 2. Financial Assistance Limits & Disbursements
- **Maximum Limit Per Braveheart:** **₹25 Lakh** per martyr (revised upward from ₹15 Lakh on October 10, 2023).
- **Direct Credit:** Donations made for an individual martyr are credited directly into the bank account of the designated Next of Kin (NoK).
- **General Corpus Fund:** If donations for an individual exceed ₹25 Lakh, or if contributors choose the general corpus, funds are deposited into the "Bharat Ke Veer Corpus", which is managed by a high-level committee comprising the Union Home Secretary, Director Generals of CAPFs, and eminent public trustees.

[Bharat Ke Veer Corpus Fund]
by a high-level committee comprising the Union Home Secretary, Director Generals of CAPFs, and eminent public trustees.
- **Minimum Guaranteed Entitlement:** The Trust guarantees that the NoK of every operational martyr receives a combined minimum total entitlement of **₹1 Crore** when taking into account Central ex-gratia, state ex-gratia, risk fund, and Bharat Ke Veer assistance.
- **Support for Parents of Married Martyrs:** As per the policy amendment effective May 1, 2020, parents of married martyrs receive an additional financial grant of **₹10 Lakh** from the Bharat Ke Veer corpus to ensure their long-term sustenance.

3. Central Industrial Security Force (CISF)
4. Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP)
5. Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB)
6. Assam Rifles (AR)
7. National Security Guard (NSG)

## 4. Verification & Tax Exemption
- All recipient profiles and casualty details are verified and authenticated by the Directorate General of the respective force.
